note: Chores, content v3 (10 words). Category Home Daily Life, unit Chores. Level is a plain A2 difficulty — no course level yet.

words.meaning: To clean carpets and floors with an electric machine that sucks up dust and dirt.
situations: Every Saturday, Ali plugs in the noisy machine and pushes it over the living-room carpet to suck up crumbs.
The cat hides under the bed whenever the loud cleaning machine is switched on.
gaps: I need to ______ the carpet — there are crumbs everywhere.
Can you ______ the stairs while I clean the kitchen?
She ______s the bedroom every weekend.
hints: Cleaning with an electric machine that sucks up dirt.
Six letters with a double 'u'.

commonMistakes.sentence: I vacuumed the floor with a broom.
commonMistakes.correction: I swept the floor with a broom. / I vacuumed the floor.
commonMistakes.why: You 'vacuum' with an electric machine; with a broom you 'sweep'.

words.meaning: To make clothes smooth and remove creases using a hot, flat electric tool.
situations: Before the job interview, Omar pressed his shirt with the hot tool on the board until it was smooth.
My mum always presses my school uniform on Sunday night so it has no creases.
gaps: I have to ______ my shirt before the meeting — it's full of creases.
Don't ______ that silk dress on a high heat!
He ______s his clothes every Sunday evening.
hints: Make clothes smooth with a hot tool.
Same word as a strong grey metal.

commonMistakes.sentence: I ironed my clothes in the washing machine.
commonMistakes.correction: I washed my clothes in the washing machine, then ironed them.
commonMistakes.why: You 'iron' clothes with a hot iron after washing them.

words.meaning: To clean a hard floor with water, using a stick with a wet head of cloth or strings.
situations: After the juice spilled on the kitchen tiles, Sara got a bucket of soapy water and wiped them clean with a wet stick.
The cleaner pushes a wet stick with strings across the shop's tiles every evening.
gaps: Someone spilled juice in the kitchen, so I need to ______.
After sweeping, don't forget to ______ with soapy water.
The cleaner will ______ before the shop opens.
hints: Clean hard floors with water and a wet stick.
Three words: a cleaning tool used as a verb + 'the floor'.

commonMistakes.why: You mop hard floors with water; carpets are vacuumed.

words.meaning: To clean dust and dirt from a floor by brushing it with a broom.
situations: After the party, Dad brushed all the crumbs and confetti into a pile with a broom and a dustpan.
Every morning, the shopkeeper brushes the dust and leaves away from his shop's doorstep.
gaps: Can you ______ the kitchen floor? There's sand everywhere.
He ______s the yard every morning with an old broom.
______ the dust into the dustpan and throw it away.
hints: Brush dirt off the floor with a broom.
Five letters; past tense 'swept'.

words.meaning: To wipe the thin grey powder off tables, shelves and other furniture with a cloth or duster.
situations: Mona wiped the thin grey layer off the bookshelves and the TV table with a soft cloth.
Before the guests came, Grandma ran a soft cloth over every shelf and table until they shone.
gaps: The shelves look grey — it's time to ______.
Can you ______ in the living room before the guests arrive?
I ______ with a soft cloth once a week.
hints: Wipe the grey powder off tables and shelves.
Three words: a word for grey powder (as a verb) + 'the furniture'.

commonMistakes.sentence: I dusted off the floor with a mop.
commonMistakes.correction: I dusted the furniture with a cloth.
commonMistakes.why: You dust furniture with a cloth or duster; floors are swept or mopped.

words.meaning: To wash the plates, cups, pots and cutlery after a meal.
situations: After dinner, my brother fills the sink with hot soapy water and washes every plate and glass.
There's a pile of dirty pots and cups in the sink — whose turn is it?
gaps: You cooked, so I'll ______ tonight.
Whose turn is it to ______ after lunch?
He never helps me ______ — the sink is always full.
hints: Wash everything you ate and cooked with.
Three words: 'do the' + a word for plates.

commonMistakes.why: We 'do' the dishes, not 'make' them ('make' is for cooking).

words.meaning: To pull the sheets and covers straight and tidy on a bed after sleeping in it.
situations: Every morning, Lina straightens her blanket, puts her pillows in place and smooths the cover.
The hotel cleaner tidied the covers and fluffed the pillows while we were at breakfast.
gaps: ______ before you go to school, please.
In the army, you must ______ perfectly every morning.
I always ______ as soon as I get up.
hints: Tidy your blanket and pillows after sleeping.
Three words: 'make the' + where you sleep.

commonMistakes.sentence: I did my bed this morning.
commonMistakes.correction: I made my bed this morning.

words.meaning: To take the dirty sheets off a bed and put clean ones on.
situations: Every Sunday, Ahmed pulls off the old bedding, puts it in the wash and puts fresh, clean ones on.
The guest is coming tomorrow, so Mum is putting fresh bedding on the spare bed.
gaps: The bed smells a bit — it's time to ______.
Hotels ______ every day for new guests.
I ______ once a week and wash the old ones.
hints: Put clean bedding on the bed.
Three words: 'change the' + the cloth you sleep on.

commonMistakes.sentence: I changed the bed sheet clean.
commonMistakes.why: Just say 'change the sheets' — it already means putting clean ones on.

words.meaning: To give flowers and plants water so they can grow.
situations: Before going on holiday, Sara asked her neighbour to give her flowers a drink every two days.
Grandpa fills his green can every evening and gives each pot on the balcony a drink.
gaps: Can you ______ while I'm on holiday?
The leaves are brown — did you forget to ______?
I ______ on the balcony every evening.
hints: Give green things in pots a drink.
Three words: 'water the' + things that grow in pots.

words.meaning: To wash, dry and fold your dirty clothes and towels.
situations: On Saturdays, Omar sorts his dirty clothes by colour, puts them in the machine and hangs them up to dry.
The basket of dirty clothes is full, so Mona carries it to the washing machine.
gaps: I have no clean socks — I need to ______.
My roommate and I take turns to ______ every week.
She uses the machines downstairs to ______.
hints: Wash and dry your dirty clothes.
Three words: 'do the' + a word for dirty clothes.

commonMistakes.sentence: I need to make the laundry.
commonMistakes.correction: I need to do the laundry.
